chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hulwani, from Abu Ismail al-Sayqal al-Razi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In Paradise there is a tree called al-Muzn. When God Mighty and Majestic intends to create a believer, a drop falls from it. It does not touch any vegetable, nor any fruit, nor any date, which either a believer or a disbeliever eats from it, except that God Mighty and Majestic brings forth from his loins a believer.

key_terms.الْمُزْنُ: al-Muzn — a tree in Paradise whose name means 'rain cloud' or 'nimbus'; its drops carry the divine decree of faith
key_terms.تَقَاطَرَتْ: dripped/trickled — the falling of a sacred drop from the tree
key_terms.صُلْبِهِ: from his loins/back — the lineage or progeny of the person who consumed the drop

ai.seo_question: What is the tree al-Muzn in Paradise and how does it relate to the creation of believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes the cosmic origin of faith: in Paradise there is a tree called al-Muzn (the Rain Cloud), and when God decrees the creation of a believer, a sacred drop falls from it and enters the food chain. Whoever eats from something touched by this drop — whether believer or unbeliever — will have a believing offspring brought forth from their lineage. This hadith underscores that iman (faith) has a divine, pre-worldly origin and is not simply the product of human choice alone, reflecting the Shia theological emphasis on divine decree and the innate disposition (fitra) toward belief.
